sections.skill: Ask for clarifying questions or stated assumptions

questions.domain: Foundation 4: Asking for what you need
questions.prompt: In this fictional example, what did the response do with missing details?

choices.text: It guessed the guest count, budget and place
It listed its assumptions clearly at the top
It asked clarifying questions first
It refused to answer the request

questions.correct_answer: It guessed the guest count, budget and place
questions.intro: When a request is missing information, a tool usually fills the gaps with GUESSES, and it may not tell you it guessed. You can change that. Ask it to ASK CLARIFYING QUESTIONS first ("Before you answer, ask me up to three questions about anything unclear"), or to STATE ITS ASSUMPTIONS ("List any assumptions you made at the top"). Both make hidden guesses visible so you can correct them. This is especially useful when details matter, such as dates, budgets, audiences or rules, and when you are not sure what information the tool needs.
questions.feedback: Gaps were filled with unstated guesses.

sections.skill: Spot what information is missing from a request

questions.domain: Foundation 4: Asking for what you need
questions.prompt: "Book a table for dinner." Which detail is missing?

choices.text: That it is a booking
That a table is wanted
That it is for dinner
How many people and when

questions.correct_answer: How many people and when
questions.intro: A quick way to find gaps is to ask the "W" questions about a request: WHO is it for or about? WHAT exactly is needed? WHEN is it due or happening? WHERE? HOW MUCH (budget, length, number)? Any important "W" with no answer is a gap the tool will fill by guessing. Example: "Book a table for dinner" is missing who (how many people), when (date and time) and where (which area or restaurant).

sections.skill: Close the gaps only you can fill

questions.domain: Foundation 4: Asking for what you need
questions.prompt: The tool asks three questions and the user replies, "Whatever you think." What will happen?

choices.text: The answers will be verified automatically
The tool will refuse to continue
The tool will still have to guess
The tool will know the right answers

questions.correct_answer: The tool will still have to guess
questions.intro: Clarifying questions are only useful if you answer them. And stated assumptions are only useful if you read them: an assumption like "I assumed the budget is 500 dollars" may be the single most important line in the answer. Be careful with the opposite problem too: if you answer "whatever you think," the tool will still guess. Some answers depend on facts only you know, such as your own deadline or a school's rules. When a gap involves such facts, supply them rather than letting the tool invent them.
